# Strict Style Hook

Enforces project styling rules on code generated by AI agents. The hook warns or blocks changes that:

- Use hex color literals (e.g. `#fff`, `#1a2b3c`) instead of design tokens/variables
- Use arbitrary Tailwind values (e.g. `text-[18px]`, `w-[123px]`)
- Include inline numeric style values in `style` attributes (e.g. `style={{ margin: 12 }}` or `style="font-size:12px"`)
- Contain duplicated or unsorted static `className` strings (auto-fixed by the validator)

This hook is intended to run automatically for all Copilot/agent-generated code and can be configured to `warn` or `block` commits or session writes.

## Overview

The hook consists of:

- `strict-style-hook.json` — hook configuration (placed at repository root `.github/hooks/`)
- `validate-generated.sh` — shell wrapper that runs the Node validator
- `validate-generated.js` — Node validator that detects violations and auto-fixes static `className` strings

## Features

- Detects hex color literals, inline numeric style values (px/rem/em/vh/vw), and Tailwind arbitrary values
- Auto-deduplicates and alphabetically sorts static `className="..."` values
- Configurable behavior via the hook JSON (`block` vs `warn`) and environment variables
- Scans only relevant file types: `.ts`,`.tsx`,`.js`,`.jsx`,`.css`,`.scss`

## Installation

1. Copy the hook files into your repository (already present in this template):

```bash
cp -r hooks/strict-style-hook .github/hooks/
```

2. Make the shell wrapper executable:

```bash
chmod +x .github/hooks/validate-generated.sh
```

3. Commit the hook to the repository default branch so agent hooks can find it.

## Configuration

Example `strict-style-hook.json` (placed at `.github/hooks/strict-style-hook.json`):

```json
{
  "name": "strict-style-enforcer",
  "applyTo": ["**/*"],
  "trigger": "PreWrite",
  "when": ["CodeGeneration", "CopilotGenerated"],
  "mode": "block",
  "script": ".github/hooks/validate-generated.sh",
  "options": {
    "enforceVariableColorsOnly": true,
    "enforceTypographyTokens": true,
    "autoFixClassStrings": true
  }
}
```

- `mode`: `block` (exit non-zero on violations) or `warn` (log only)
- `applyTo`: glob patterns to scope the hook; current default targets all files

## How it works

1. Agent invokes the hook on the configured trigger (`PreWrite` / `sessionEnd` / etc.)
2. The shell wrapper (`validate-generated.sh`) calls `validate-generated.js` with file paths (or scans `src/` when no args)
3. The validator scans each file for:
   - Hex color literals (`#abc`, `#aabbcc`)
   - Tailwind arbitrary bracket values (`[...]`)
   - Inline numeric style values in `style` attributes
   - Static `className` attributes to optionally auto-fix duplicates and sort classes
4. If violations are found and `mode` is `block`, the validator exits with non-zero status to prevent the write/commit.

## Example usage

Run the shell wrapper against a file or let the hook run automatically:

```bash
# Scan specific file(s)
.github/hooks/validate-generated.sh src/components/features/contact/ContactForm.tsx

# Scan the entire src/ tree (wrapper will do this when no args)
.github/hooks/validate-generated.sh
```

If violations are detected, the script prints friendly error messages with the offending patterns. Static `className="..."` occurrences may be auto-fixed in-place; other violations must be addressed manually (replace hex with tokens, remove arbitrary values, move numeric styles to tokens or CSS variables).

## Customization

- Extend `validate-generated.js` to support token mapping (auto-replace hex -> variable) — requires a `tokens.json` mapping file.
- Change `mode` to `warn` in the hook JSON to avoid blocking commits while still surfacing issues.
- Add CI job or pre-commit hook to run the validator as part of the pipeline (recommended).

## Disabling

To temporarily disable the hook:

- Set environment variable `SKIP_STRICT_STYLE=true` in the hook invocation environment, or
- Remove or edit the `when`/`applyTo` entries in the hook JSON.

## Limitations

- Pattern-based checks; may produce false positives for example/test fixtures
- Auto-fix is conservative: it only modifies static `className="..."` strings and does not attempt complex AST rewrites
- Does not currently auto-convert hex colors to token names — this requires a maintained token map

## Next steps (suggested)

- Add a `tokens.json` mapping and optionally enable automatic color token replacement
- Add a CI job that runs the validator on pull requests
- Add small unit tests or example files demonstrating both blocked violations and successful fixes (I can add these for you)
